title: Roman Roads and the Connected Empire

activity_visual_value.rationale: Concept map prepares learners to notice road-system relationships before classification.
Process visual supports inspecting construction stages before completing the sequence task.
Comparison framework supports road-type discrimination before the ranking task.

visual_affordances.subject: Roman road network relationships
visual_affordances.context: Visual brief: help learners notice how roads, forts, and supply nodes relate before they classify network roles; show labelled structural links without revealing the completed classification.
allowed_claims: Road networks connect military and economic nodes.
disallowed_claims: All Roman roads served only military purposes.
visual_affordances.rationale: Prepare noticing and sorting before the classification task.
visual_affordances.pedagogical_added_value: Adds relational cues for network roles without revealing conclusions.
visual_affordances.reasoning_supported: Learners notice and sort relationships before classifying.

visual_affordances.subject: Roman road construction stages
visual_affordances.context: Visual brief: show the ordered construction process so learners can inspect stages before completing the sequence reasoning task; do not reveal worked answers.
allowed_claims: Road construction proceeds through layered stages.
visual_affordances.rationale: Support process inspection before learners complete the sequencing task.
visual_affordances.pedagogical_added_value: Makes stage order inspectable without completing the learner sequence.
visual_affordances.reasoning_supported: Learners inspect process structure before completing sequence reasoning.
visual_affordances.canonical_discipline_note: Show stages as inspectable structure, not answered worksheet.

visual_affordances.subject: Types and functions of Roman roads
visual_affordances.context: Visual brief: compare road types and functions so learners can identify discriminating features before ranking or classifying examples.
allowed_claims: Roman roads differ by function and construction class.
disallowed_claims: All road types are functionally identical.
visual_affordances.rationale: Support comparison before the learner ranking task.
visual_affordances.pedagogical_added_value: Adds comparison dimensions without revealing rankings.
visual_affordances.reasoning_supported: Learners compare before completing ranking conclusions.

visual_affordances.subject: Knowledge Summary of imperial connectivity
visual_affordances.context: Visual brief: after Knowledge Summary prose, consolidate how road types, construction process, and network roles support imperial connectivity; synthesise conclusions already developed in the summary.
disallowed_claims: Causal claims not present in the knowledge summary.
visual_affordances.rationale: Knowledge Summary benefits from a consolidation visual after reasoning.
visual_affordances.reasoning_supported: Connect road types, process, and network roles after analysis.

activities.learner_task: Classify Roman road network relationships using the scenario cards.

overview.body: This self-study resource explores Roman roads and imperial connectivity.

learning_purpose.body: Learners analyse road types, construction process, and network roles.

knowledge_summary.body: Roman roads supported imperial connectivity through differentiated road types, staged construction, and networked military-economic nodes.
